messages:
dev_mike: Hey support — seeing clients hit 429 mid-stream on SSE. Dashboard shows ~600 tokens billed but client only received ~250 tokens. Started after we rolled out per-user quotas. Repro: raw SSE from node-fetch EventSource polyfill, long completion (>500 tokens) gets cut with a 429 about 30s in. request_id=r12345-20260203T15:04Z.

alice_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact request_id/timestamps, sample curl, and whether this is SDK or raw SSE? Need to loop in billing and eng.

dev_mike: request_id: r12345-20260203T15:04Z, timestamp 2026-02-03T15:04:05Z. Raw SSE. Minimal repro below (key redacted):

curl --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "X-User-Id: 42" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2B-quant","max_tokens":1024,"temperature":0.2,"stream":true,"prompt":"<long prompt>"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions/stream

Client stream shows deltas then an error event: 
[data: {"delta":"..."}]
[data: {"delta":"..."}]
[data: {"error":{"message":"quota exceeded","code":429}}]

Server returned headers: x-rw-retry-after:30, x-rw-request-id: r12345

bob_engineer: Thanks. Two initial hypotheses: (1) quota accounting pre-reserves or estimates full completion (e.g., fallback path or estimator) and later the live stream emits less; (2) auth/rotation issues causing additional internal retries or duplicate accounting on reconnection. Do you rotate short-lived bearer tokens per request?

dev_mike: We mint short-lived tokens (1h TTL) but they don't rotate mid-request. Also observed no client-side reconnect until after the 429. Server logs attached below.

dev_mike: Server log snippet:
```
[2026-02-03T15:04:05Z] request=r12345 state=streaming tokens_emitted=248 kv_cache=hit
[2026-02-03T15:04:35Z] request=r12345 rate_limiter=blocked reason=quota_exceeded account=acct_987 tokens_counted=600
[2026-02-03T15:04:35Z] request=r12345 connection_closed client_cause=client_disconnect? false
```
carla_billing: tokens_counted=600 vs tokens_emitted=248 suggests either pre-reservation (full max_tokens) or that a fallback/internal non-streaming call charged full completion. We saw this pattern before when the runtime triggered an internal 'completion_fallback' that reserved the remaining tokens. Can you check traces for any internal fallback or non-streaming call tied to r12345?

dev_mike: I found an internal call right before the rate_limiter block: internal_call=completion_fallback for r12345. Not surface-level in client's stream. I uploaded full trace to secure storage (redacted).

bob_engineer: That sounds like the cause — when fallback runs, accounting may reserve the predicted full token usage. If the live SSE then terminates early, reconciliation isn't decrementing the reservation. Also reconnections may open new reservations before old ones release. Two action items: (A) reconcile reservation vs actual consumption on stream termination; (B) ensure reconnection doesn't double-count.

alice_support: For immediate customer relief: we can issue a provisional credit/refund while eng investigates. @carla_billing can you open a billing adjustment and track it to incident? We'll let the customer know we're investigating and will refund discrepancy.

carla_billing: Opening ticket BILL-INC-2026-45. Please attach CSV of token_delta events for acct_987 and the request_id. I'll need the quota window and estimated billed amount.

dev_mike: Uploaded debug trace: s3://redwood-debug/20260203/r12345.trace (internal link). Note: unrelated 401 seen in a separate test earlier but not for this request. Also noticed some clients reconnect with Connection: close -> new SSE; that sequence may create overlapping reservations if previous connection wasn't released promptly. Adding to repro harness.

bob_engineer: Agreed. Engineering plan: ENG-STREAM-433 — investigate reservation flow on fallback; add reconciliation to decrement reserved tokens when stream closes before reserved amount consumed; add a metric alert when tokens_accounted - tokens_emitted > 200 for a single request. Also ensure reservations are tied to connection_id and released on close. I'll open PR with tests against the Node repro harness.

alice_support: Thanks — dev_mike, can you share the customer-facing wording? We'll tell ACME Chat: "We've opened an investigation and provisionally credited the account while we fix a token accounting bug that can over-report billed tokens for streaming requests when fallback or reconnection occurs." Keep us posted.

oncall_bot: Incident created ENG-STREAM-433 by bob_engineer. Severity:P2. Thread pinned.

dev_mike: Quick note for repro: try a long prompt with max_tokens large, force an internal fallback by toggling a kernel path, and then close the connection abruptly. Reconnecting client-side has reproduced double-counting locally. I'll add the node harness to the incident.

bob_engineer: Good repro notes. We'll prioritize a fix for reserving tokens atomically and adding reconciliation on disconnect.

alice_support: Closing loop for now. We'll update customer once billing adjustment is created and eng posts a root-cause. :thumbsup:
